title: 'Excited delirium' blamed
article: A study into Taser use by the Victoria Police Department in 2005 found some deaths associated with Tasers occur in people suffering from "excited delirium."
People with the condition -- often those suffering from mental illness or users of cocaine or methamphetamines -- are violent, paranoid and out of control.

The report recommended someone who has been Tasered should be restrained face-up, or in a way that makes it easy to breathe quickly. Those who have struggled with police or are suffering from excited delirium have higher than normal levels of carbon dioxide in their blood, putting them at risk of a heart attack. Breathing quickly helps reduce the levels of C02 .

At an inquest earlier this year into the 2004 death of Robert Bagnell, 44, who died after being hit by a Vancouver police Taser, the jury ruled he died from a "restraint-associated cardiac arrest as a result of acute cocaine intoxication and psychosis."

Another B.C. coroner's jury found cocaine to be the cause of death -- not a Taser shot -- in the May 2004 death of Roman Andreichikov. He suffered a fatal heart attack while in a cocaine- induced psychosis. The personal trainer was Tasered while struggling with police.
